model.ecommerce.int_orders_enriched.raw_code:
with orders as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_orders') }}

),

customers as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

order_items as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_order_items_aggregated') }}

),

payments as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_payments') }}

),

shipments as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_shipments_enriched') }}

),

reviews as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_reviews') }}

),

enriched as (

    select
        -- =====================================================
        -- Pedido
        -- =====================================================

        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_at,
        o.order_status,
        o.shipping_type,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Cliente
        -- =====================================================

        c.state as customer_state,
        c.birth_date as customer_birth_date,
        c.created_at as customer_created_at,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Itens
        -- =====================================================

        oi.item_count,
        oi.distinct_products,
        oi.total_quantity,
        oi.gross_amount,
        oi.discount_amount,
        oi.net_amount,
        oi.total_weight_kg,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Pagamento
        -- =====================================================

        p.payment_id,
        p.payment_method,
        p.payment_amount,
        p.installments,
        p.payment_status,
        p.paid_at,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Logística
        -- =====================================================

        s.shipment_id,
        s.shipped_at,
        s.estimated_delivery_at,
        s.delivered_at,
        s.delivery_duration,
        s.is_delayed,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Avaliação
        -- =====================================================

        r.review_id,
        r.rating,
        r.reviewed_at

    from orders o

    left join customers c
        on o.customer_id = c.customer_id

    left join order_items oi
        on o.order_id = oi.order_id

    left join payments p
        on o.order_id = p.order_id

    left join shipments s
        on o.order_id = s.order_id

    left join reviews r
        on o.order_id = r.order_id

)

select *
from enriched

model.ecommerce.int_order_items_aggregat.raw_code:
with order_items as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_order_items_enriched') }}

),

aggregated as (

    select
        order_id,

        count(*) as item_count,
        count(distinct product_id) as distinct_products,
        sum(quantity) as total_quantity,

        sum(gross_amount) as gross_amount,
        sum(discount_amount) as discount_amount,
        sum(net_amount) as net_amount,

        sum(
            weight_kg * quantity
        ) as total_weight_kg

    from order_items

    group by order_id

)

select *
from aggregated

order_item_id.name: order_item_id
order_item_id.description: Identificador único do item de pedido.

weight_kg.name: weight_kg
weight_kg.description: Peso unitário do produto em quilogramas.

discount_pct.description: Percentual de desconto aplicado ao item.

gross_amount.name: gross_amount

net_amount.description: Valor líquido do item após o desconto.

model.ecommerce.int_order_items_enriched.raw_code:
with order_items as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_order_items') }}

),

products as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_products') }}

),

enriched as (

    select
        oi.order_item_id,
        oi.order_id,
        oi.product_id,
        p.category,
        p.brand,
        p.weight_kg,
        oi.quantity,
        oi.unit_price,
        oi.discount_pct,
        oi.quantity * oi.unit_price
            as gross_amount,
        oi.quantity
            * oi.unit_price
            * oi.discount_pct
            as discount_amount,
        oi.quantity
            * oi.unit_price
            * (1 - oi.discount_pct)
            as net_amount

    from order_items oi
    left join products p
        on oi.product_id = p.product_id

)

select *
from enriched

model.ecommerce.int_shipments_enriched.raw_code:
with shipments as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_shipments') }}

),

enriched as (

    select
        shipment_id,
        order_id,
        shipped_at,
        estimated_delivery_at,
        delivered_at,

        delivered_at - shipped_at
            as delivery_duration,

        case
            when delivered_at is null then null

            when delivered_at > estimated_delivery_at
                then true

            else false
        end as is_delayed

    from shipments

)

select *
from enriched

model.ecommerce.fct_daily_sales.raw_code:
with orders as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_orders_enriched') }}

),

daily as (

    select
        order_at::date as order_date,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Volume
        -- =====================================================

        count(*) as total_orders,

        count(*) filter (
            where order_status <> 'cancelled'
        ) as valid_orders,

        count(*) filter (
            where order_status = 'cancelled'
        ) as cancelled_orders,

        count(distinct customer_id) as total_customers,

        sum(
            case
                when order_status <> 'cancelled'
                    then total_quantity
                else 0
            end
        ) as total_units,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Financeiro
        -- =====================================================

        sum(
            case
                when order_status <> 'cancelled'
                    then gross_amount
                else 0
            end
        ) as gross_amount,

        sum(
            case
                when order_status <> 'cancelled'
                    then discount_amount
                else 0
            end
        ) as discount_amount,

        sum(
            case
                when order_status <> 'cancelled'
                    then net_amount
                else 0
            end
        ) as net_amount,

        -- =====================================================
        -- Experiência / Operação
        -- =====================================================

        count(*) filter (
            where is_delayed = true
        ) as delayed_orders,

        count(*) filter (
            where delivered_at is not null
        ) as delivered_orders,

        count(rating) as reviewed_orders,

        avg(rating) as avg_rating

    from orders

    group by 1

),

final as (

    select
        *,

        {{ safe_divide('net_amount', 'valid_orders') }}
            as avg_order_value,

        {{ safe_divide('cancelled_orders', 'total_orders') }}
            as cancellation_rate,

        {{ safe_divide('delayed_orders', 'delivered_orders') }}
            as delay_rate,

        {{ safe_divide('reviewed_orders', 'total_orders') }}
            as review_rate

    from daily

)

select *
from final

{{
    config(
        materialized='incremental',
        unique_key='order_id',
        incremental_strategy='merge'
    )
}}

with orders as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_orders_enriched') }}

    {% if is_incremental() %}

        where order_at >= (
            select
                max(order_at) - interval '30 days'
            from {{ this }}
        )

    {% endif %}

),

final as (

    select
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        order_at,
        order_status,
        shipping_type,
        customer_state,
        customer_birth_date,
        customer_created_at,
        item_count,
        distinct_products,
        total_quantity,
        gross_amount,
        discount_amount,
        net_amount,
        total_weight_kg,
        payment_id,
        payment_method,
        payment_amount,
        installments,
        payment_status,
        paid_at,
        shipment_id,
        shipped_at,
        estimated_delivery_at,
        delivered_at,
        delivery_duration,
        is_delayed,
        review_id,
        rating,
        reviewed_at

    from orders

)

select *
from final

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.name: postgres__get_relations
macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_relations() -%}

  {#
      -- in pg_depend, objid is the dependent, refobjid is the referenced object
      --  > a pg_depend entry indicates that the referenced object cannot be
      --  > dropped without also dropping the dependent object.
  #}

  {%- call statement('relations', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select distinct
        dependent_namespace.nspname as dependent_schema,
        dependent_class.relname as dependent_name,
        referenced_namespace.nspname as referenced_schema,
        referenced_class.relname as referenced_name

    -- Query for views: views are entries in pg_class with an entry in pg_rewrite, but we avoid
    -- a seq scan on pg_rewrite by leveraging the fact there is an "internal" row in pg_depend for
    -- the view...
    from pg_class as dependent_class
    join pg_namespace as dependent_namespace on dependent_namespace.oid = dependent_class.relnamespace
    join pg_depend as dependent_depend on dependent_depend.refobjid = dependent_class.oid
        and dependent_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.deptype = 'i'

    -- ... and via pg_depend (that has a row per column, hence the need for "distinct" above, and
    -- making sure to exclude the internal row to avoid a view appearing to depend on itself)...
    join pg_depend as joining_depend on joining_depend.objid = dependent_depend.objid
        and joining_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refobjid != dependent_depend.refobjid

    -- ... we can find the tables they query from in pg_class, but excluding system tables. Note we
    -- don't need need to exclude _dependent_ system tables, because they only query from other
    -- system tables, and so are automatically excluded by excluding _referenced_ system tables
    join pg_class as referenced_class on referenced_class.oid = joining_depend.refobjid
    join pg_namespace as referenced_namespace on referenced_namespace.oid = referenced_class.relnamespace
        and referenced_namespace.nspname != 'information_schema'
        and referenced_namespace.nspname not like 'pg\_%'

    order by
        dependent_schema, dependent_name, referenced_schema, referenced_name;

  {%- endcall -%}

  {{ return(load_result('relations').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

{% macro postgres__list_relations_without_caching(schema_relation) %}
  {% call statement('list_relations_without_caching', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      tablename as name,

    from pg_tables
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      viewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,

      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      matviewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,

    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select distinct
     '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
     proname as name,
     ns.nspname as schema,
     'function' as type
    from pg_proc
     join pg_namespace as ns on pronamespace = ns.oid
    where ns.nspname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
  {% endcall %}

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_show_in.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_show_indexes_sql(relation) %}
    select
        i.relname                                   as name,
        m.amname                                    as method,
        ix.indisunique                              as "unique",
        array_to_string(array_agg(a.attname), ',')  as column_names
    from pg_index ix
    join pg_class i
        on i.oid = ix.indexrelid
    join pg_am m
        on m.oid=i.relam
    join pg_class t
        on t.oid = ix.indrelid
    join pg_namespace n
        on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    join pg_attribute a
        on a.attrelid = t.oid
        and a.attnum = ANY(ix.indkey)
    where t.relname = '{{ relation.identifier }}'
      and n.nspname = '{{ relation.schema }}'
      and t.relkind in ('r', 'm')
    group by 1, 2, 3
    order by 1, 2, 3
{% endmacro %}

doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
